premise: I spent three decades as my father’s live‑in caregiver, forgoing my nursing career, only for my sister—the golden child who never lifted a finger—to forge a will after his death and steal my $240,000 inheritance; I found the true will taped behind his favorite portrait, contested probate, reclaimed the house, and now run “Heirloom of Deceit Estate Sales” from its parlor, where she dusts antiques in an apron that says “Wiped Away the Truth” and every item’s price tag prints her probate‑fraud docket number.
